votes.reasoning: unmark (NotificationService.swift:284-296) now only acts on a crossing that still has a pending entry. Delivered crossings have none (delivered() removes it), so a delivered mark is never touched. I traced three cases. Case 1, 70 and 90 both in flight, 70 fails first: highest is 90, not 70, so the chain rewrites pending[90].previous from 70 to nil. When 90 then fails, highest becomes nil, and the next 75 reading re-sends 70. Case 2, reverse order: 90 fails and restores highest to 70, then 70 fails and sets it to nil. Case 3, 90 fails and then 70 is delivered: highest stays 70, with no duplicate. That matches the higher_failure_keeps_lower_in_flight_mark test. Reversal to round 1 turned double_failure_does_not_restore_undelivered_mark RED (last is 5h.90); restored after.

Tracker complexity: unmark (NotificationService.swift:284-295) is 12 lines. Its deepest nesting is 3 (func, else, for-where), with 1 guard-let and 1 if/else. Tracking a Pending record per threshold (:258, with previous and parked) is the smallest structure that can express 'restore the nearest mark that was not itself a failure'. A single scalar cannot do that, so this is not a speculative abstraction. The pending entries are cleared at every place the key dies: reset (:341) and prune (:363). Delivered entries are dropped at :298-301, so the map does not grow without bound. Minor duplication added by the diff, not blocking: the line 'if pending[key]?.isEmpty ?? false { pending.removeValue(forKey: key) }' appears twice (:294, :301). Also, the reset and prune branches now each repeat the same 3 removeValue calls (highestNotified, missedSnapshots, pending). Both belong in new_findings.

The pending map in NotificationThresholdTracker is internal state. It is dropped on reset and prune, next to highestNotified and missedSnapshots, so it adds no new growing structure beyond what the existing prune already bounds. The Crossing typealias shrinks back to (window, threshold), and unmark(restoring:) is gone. Both are internal to the app target, and the only other caller, NotificationThresholdTrackerTests, was updated in the same diff. Nothing is serialized or persisted.
